gloss: celebratory meal; festive tray of dishes

definitions.gloss: celebratory meal; festive tray of dishes
definitions.explanation: A special set of dishes served to mark an occasion such as a birth, a wedding, a milestone birthday, or New Year. {膳|ぜん} is the individual tray on which a formal Japanese meal is laid out, so the word names both the food and its presentation.

examples.japanese: {祝|いわ}い{膳|ぜん}を{用意|ようい}する。
{赤|あか}ちゃんのお{食|く}い{初|ぞ}めに{祝|いわ}い{膳|ぜん}を{並|なら}べた。
examples.english: We laid out a celebratory meal for the baby's first-food ceremony.

examples.japanese: {結婚|けっこん}が{決|き}まったと{伝|つた}えると、{祖母|そぼ}は{祝|いわ}い{膳|ぜん}を{作|つく}って{待|ま}っていてくれた。
examples.english: When I told her the wedding was settled, my grandmother had a celebratory meal waiting for me.

examples.japanese: {祝|いわ}い{膳|ぜん}には{鯛|たい}や{赤飯|せきはん}など、めでたいとされる{料理|りょうり}が{並|なら}ぶ。
examples.english: A celebratory meal features auspicious dishes such as sea bream and red rice.

notes:
Belongs to the vocabulary of family ceremonies rather than restaurants, and is usually something prepared or ordered at home for an occasion.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {祝|いわ}い{膳|ぜん}を{用意|ようい}する: to prepare a celebratory meal
- {祝|いわ}い{膳|ぜん}を{囲|かこ}む: to gather around a celebratory meal
- お{食|く}い{初|ぞ}めの{祝|いわ}い{膳|ぜん}: the meal for a baby's first-food ceremony

CULTURAL NOTE:
The dishes are chosen for their auspicious associations: {鯛|たい} (sea bream) for めでたい, {赤飯|せきはん} (red rice) for celebration, and whole fish or foods served in pairs for completeness.
